description: Links zoning bylaw to existing tree protection bylaw.
Removes redundant underground construction restrictions for infill housing.
Allows underground construction in setbacks without existing trees.

chips.text: First reading passed (9-0)
9 for, 0 against
Mayor Block questions if amendment erodes tree protection, seeking clarity on redundancy.
Residents of Nutana and Varsity View neighborhoods are concerned.
Council questioned administration's public engagement process and Home Builders' role.
City lacks bylaws on underground parkade ramp slopes and low-impact construction.
Community associations opposed; Home Builders' Association supported the amendment.
Amendment impacts urban forest, affecting air quality, shade, and habitat.
Pilot project will track urban forestry staff time for permit reviews.

segments.title: Staff Report on Zoning Bylaw Amendment
segments.takeaway: Administration presented the proposed amendment to link the zoning bylaw with the tree protection bylaw, developed with urban forestry and home builders.

segments.title: Municipal Planning Commission Report
segments.takeaway: The Municipal Planning Commission recommended approval of the proposed amendments, supporting the balance between urban forestry protection and development viability.

segments.title: SOS Trees Coalition Presentation
segments.takeaway: Tom Gold from SOS Trees Coalition opposed the amendment, arguing it would damage large trees and compromise the urban forest, despite its stated intent.

segments.title: Barcyvian Community Association Presentation
segments.takeaway: Jonathan Nailer from Barcyvian Community Association opposed the amendment, citing lack of public consultation, potential tree damage, and biased decision-making processes.

segments.title: Nutana Community Association Presentation
segments.takeaway: Mr. Kloberton from Nutana Community Association opposed the amendment, raising concerns about inadequate public consultation, threats to the urban forest, and impacts of front access underground parki

segments.title: Home Builder Association Presentation
segments.takeaway: Nicole Berges from the Home Builder Association supported the amendment, stating it corrects an unnecessary regulation and eliminates red tape while existing tree protection bylaws remain.

segments.title: Public Comment on Construction Impacts
segments.takeaway: Douglas Thompson raised concerns about underground parkade ramp slopes and the need for low-impact construction to protect adjacent properties and trees.

segments.title: Questions for Administration
segments.takeaway: Councillors questioned administration on stakeholder engagement, urban forestry's role in permitting, and the necessity of the amendment given existing tree protection bylaws.

segments.title: Motion to Receive Reports
segments.takeaway: Council moved to receive the reports related to the Zoning Bylaw Text Amendment.

segments.title: Motion to Close Hearing
segments.takeaway: Council voted to close the public hearing for the Zoning Bylaw Text Amendment.

segments.title: Motion for Second Reading
segments.takeaway: Council moved and approved the second reading of the bylaw for the Zoning Bylaw Text Amendment.

segments.title: Motion for Third Reading
segments.takeaway: Council moved and approved the third reading of the bylaw, completing the approval process for the amendment.
